claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large magnetocaloric and barocaloric response but poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
Approximately 0.2 at% interstitial carbon should be introduced during processing of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Carbon addition followed by optimized heat treatment will cause in situ formation of coherent nanoscale carbide precipitates.
The carbide precipitates will be distributed along grain boundaries and within the alloy matrix.
Interstitial carbon will increase the local stacking-fault energy of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Carbide precipitates will inhibit dislocation motion.
The proposed carbide precipitates will reinforce grain boundaries.
The proposed carbide precipitates will blunt crack tips.
The combined effects of crack-tip blunting and inhibited dislocation motion will enhance toughness and load-bearing integrity.
At approximately 0.2 at% carbon, fracture toughness will improve by 30–50% relative to the undoped alloy.
Carbon modification will increase the alloy's load-bearing limit relative to the undoped alloy.
The magnetocaloric response will remain within 5–10% of that of the pristine alloy.
The barocaloric response will remain within 5–10% of that of the pristine alloy.
Careful control of carbon concentration will leave the primary magneto- and barocaloric transformation largely unaltered.
The predicted benefits apply under magnetic fields of 1–3 T.
The predicted benefits apply under pressure fields up to several hundred MPa.
The predicted benefits apply near the caloric transition temperature, described as near room temperature or as otherwise tailored.
Excess carbon or nonoptimal heat treatment could cause carbide precipitates to interfere with the caloric phase transition and degrade caloric performance by more than 10%.

The hypothesis is falsified if the approximately 0.2 at% C alloy fails to improve fracture toughness by at least 30% or loses more than 10% of caloric magnitude or operational temperature range relative to the undoped control.
